newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's king confers with Mideast peace partners.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's king confers with Mideast peace partners.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein spoke by telephone on Tuesday with Middle East peace partners to help overcome obstacles to an Israeli-Palestinian deal on the West Bank town of Hebron, the official Petra news agency said.

The king conferred with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross to help facilitate a deal on an Israeli troop redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron, Petra said.
King Hussein also discussed with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak the "latest developments and coordinating efforts to help the parties to conclude a deal".

"During the contacts, there was a follow-up to efforts to conclude a deal between the Israeli and Palestinian side over the Israeli troop redeployment from Hebron and to overcome remaining obstacles," Petra said.

Israeli-PLO peace moves were on the verge of collapse when King Hussein stepped in on Sunday, flying by helicopter to Gaza and Tel Aviv to help close the gap on a date for an Israeli army pullback from rural areas in the West Bank.
Netanyahu and Arafat scheduled a meeting for late on Tuesday to try to break a deadlock over extending Palestinian rule to Hebron.
